title: Canary culture handbook and ops training (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for an internal "Canary Culture" handbook paired with hands-on ops training exercises. Goal: make cross-functional teams (product, eng, SRE, SRE-oncall, solutions) confident running progressive exposure for LLM-backed features and A/B experiments that touch routing/model selection.

Audience:
- Release leads and experiment owners
- Oncall engineers and shift stewards
- Product PMs who run behavioral ABs
- Solutions / SE for customer canaries (dedicated/private)

High-level principles (short):
- Minimize blast radius: start tiny, measure signal density, iterate.
- Signal first, anecdotes second: require defined primary/secondary signals before exposure.
- Human-in-the-loop gates for behavioral drift: include explicit human checkpoints for early waves.
- Cost-aware rollouts: route to cheaper model variants for non-critical slices.
- Fast revert is better than slow safety: plan reversion before activation.

Quick glossary (for training):
- Canary: an exposure slice of production traffic used to validate new code/model/route.
- Micro-exposure: sub-percent cohorts (0.1–0.5%) used for initial validity checks.
- Staging-sim: synthetic traffic job that exercises the same route and sequence lengths as target cohort.
- Safety net: automated detection rules + human steward action plan (escalation).

Role matrix (who does what in the run):
- Release lead (PM/Eng): defines hypothesis, success metrics, primary/secondary signals, rollback criteria.
- Steward (ops engineer): observes telemetry, executes playbook (increase/decrease/expose/revert), calls incident if signal crosses threshold.
- Model steward (applied ML): interprets quality regressions, proposes prompt changes or model pinning.
- SRE oncall: network/infra escalation, capacity adjustments, tracing/latency investigations.
- Customer success / SE (for Dedicated): communication and customer-facing rollback coordination.

Operational runbook (starter checklist):
Pre-launch (day -7 to -1):
- Hypothesis defined + owner assigned.
- Primary metric + min sample size calculated (stat power note if A/B).
- Canary signal list: latency P95, error rate, generation token cost, hallucination rate (sample-based), user satisfaction proxies.
- Synthetic staging-run created: sequence length distribution matched to live.
- Capacity check: ensure buffer for 2x modeled peak for the cohort.
- Fallback routes defined (model variant, region, capacity tier).
- Slack channel + oncall pager assigned and pre-populated with escalation links.

Activate (wave 0 -> wave N):
- Wave 0: micro-exposure (~0.1%) for 30m–2h. Rapid sanity checks only.
- Wave 1: 1% for 4–12h. Validate primary signals + perform sampling for quality.
- Wave 2+: geometric increase (1% -> 5% -> 20%) only after passing gates.
- Observation cadence: 5m alerts for infra signals, 30m sampling review for quality signals.

Guardrails (automations + thresholds):
- Infra: latency P95 > baseline + 150ms for 3 consecutive 5m buckets -> automated rollback.
- Error: 5xx rate > baseline*3 for 2m -> throttle to previous route.
- Cost: per-token cost > expected budget by 30% for sustained 30m -> notify steward and pause growth.
- Quality: automated hallucination detector flagging >3% of samples over 1h -> human review required.

Training exercises (practical labs for new stewards):
1) Simulated canary: small team runs a staged activation in a sandbox with injected latency and synthetic hallucinations. Goals: practice rollback, practice triage, update playbook.
2) Signal-hunting workshop: given a dataset of request flows, find the best slice to catch regressions early (e.g., long sequence user prompts, multi-turn rerank).
3) Rapid reversion drill: time from signal detection to full reversion under 10m (target). Run timed drills monthly.

Canary scenarios (examples to include in training):
- Model quantization regression: throughput ok but hallucination rises.
- KV cache eviction bug causing severe latency spikes for multi-turn.
- Cross-region fallback misrouting when primary region capacity full.
- Cost-surprise when a prompt amplification bug sends massive long-prompts.

Sample templates (to copy into experiment ticket):
- Hypothesis: short statement + expected direction.
- Activation plan: waves, duration, steward names, fallbacks.
- Signals: list with thresholds, owners, and action (auto/manual).
- Sampling bucket: how we select users/cohorts and rationales.

Communication playbook (who says what):
- If auto-rollback triggers: steward posts in channel with links to metrics snapshot, sample artifacts, and rollback reason.
- If manual rollback chosen: steward calls SRE oncall then notifies release lead and customer success.
- Post-mortem: 48-hour incident writeup template with short timeline, root cause hypotheses, and follow-ups.

Observation artifacts (what to capture during wave):
- Trace links for slow requests.
- 100 sampled outputs every 30m for human quality check.
- Top user intents and token length histogram.
- Cost/billing delta pipeline snapshot.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Need a lightweight RTT (request-type) taxonomy for routing decisions — draft in next week.
- Who owns the hallucination detector? ML vs Console team — tag ownership.
- Should we enforce mandatory surge budgets per release? ops + finance sync.
- Add a minimal canary simulator job in infra repo (ticket created: JIRA-4521).

Training curriculum proposal (1-day):
- Morning: 90m lecture on principles + role-play assignment. 60m signal mapping exercise.
- Lunch: 1-on-1 steward pairing signups.
- Afternoon: two 90m labs (simulated canary + reversion drill). Wrap with retrospective and playbook edits.

Quick heuristics cheatsheet (postable in Slack):
- If latency P95 spikes >20% but error rate stable -> suspect KV cache/queueing.
- If hallucination jumps but latency unchanged -> model/prompt issue, ping model steward.
- If cost sharply increases -> stop growth immediately and inspect token histograms.

References / anchors:
- LINK: Confluence signal catalog (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- JIRA-4521 (canary simulator)
- github.com/redwood-inference/experiment-sim (sandbox scripts)

Closing note (frank):
This is intentionally rough. The aim is a moldable handbook that teams can copy into their experiment ticket and a short ops training that gets folks comfortable in the chair. Biggest risk is unbalanced ownership of quality signals — need to resolve that before we make this a required checklist.

-- Aisha
(edit log: created initial sketch 2025-01-14; added training labs + thresholds 2025-02-20)
